theory: A conversation is an ordered sequence of provider messages and matched tool results, with a distinct stream for drawing incremental output. Provider adapters preserve their transport-specific continuation state, while Hardy records who enforced budgets and which usage figures were actually reported.
instead_of: Treat every provider as an interchangeable text-completion function; that would lose tool-call identity, provider-owned loop semantics, and opaque reasoning needed for continuation.

absorption.rationale: A new one-call provider fits the Provider protocol, but applying one compaction and turn-enforcement policy across both the owned loop and subscription SDK loops requires adapter-specific work.

world_mapping.rationale: Message, ToolCall, ProviderTurn, and TurnEvent distinguish conversation history from rendering and dispatch, including the call/result adjacency invariant.

abstraction.rationale: The complete-call protocol and callback-driven AgentLoop express another API transport without embedding interactive session state in it.

justification.rationale: The comments explain why original block order and opaque reasoning survive, and why an SDK budget and a harness budget must be attributed separately.

honest_limits.rationale: Provider provenance and enforcement are stated; cancellation of the owned loop is explicitly a boundary check rather than unwinding an in-flight tool.

rehearsals.requirement: Add an API transport implementing one model completion.
rehearsals.why: Implement Provider.complete and translate neutral messages; tool dispatch and budget accounting remain in AgentLoop.

rehearsals.requirement: Add a pre-call stop or steering policy.
rehearsals.why: AgentLoop already exposes before_turn and set_gate at the point where the decision belongs.

rehearsals.requirement: Make subscription SDK and owned API loops compact at exactly the same conversation boundary.
rehearsals.why: The owned loop holds the message list and compactor, while the SDK adapter delegates iteration and turn counting to the provider.
